activities.desc: Depart from PIT or connection hub. EDT → CEST (+6h)
Stroll the harbor promenade with shops, restaurants, and marina views
Munch's The Scream, Viking gold, and Norwegian art. Indoor, central, jet-lag-friendly
Karl Johans gate, Royal Palace, Akershus Fortress
Walk the sloping marble roof for iconic city + fjord views
Modern art + forest trails with panoramic Oslo Fjord views. Light hike
Oslo Mikrobryggeri, Klosteret, Det Lille Bryggeri - craft beer for the adults

groupNotes: Arrive in Oslo. Keep Day 1 light - see Jet Lag Playbook. The National Museum (The Scream) and Opera House roof are must-dos. Activities during the day help power through jet lag.

lodging.name: Citybox Oslo
lodging.pros: Self-check-in 24/7, central near Oslo Central Station, modern minimalist rooms, free Wi-Fi
lodging.cons: No breakfast, no daily housekeeping, small rooms

lodging.name: Radisson RED Oslo
lodging.pros: Modern design, excellent breakfast bar, great location near Opera House and waterfront
lodging.cons: Standard chain feel, no pool, can be noisy

lodging.name: Grand Hotel Oslo
lodging.pros: Historic 1874 property, Nobel Peace Prize venue, rooftop terrace, exceptional breakfast, prime location
lodging.cons: Very expensive, some dated rooms, tourist crowds

meals.lunch: Godt Brød coffee shop (skolebrød) or Mathallen Oslo food hall
meals.dinner: Den Glade Gris - Norwegian pork-focused gastropub (try the ribbe or nakkekoteletter). Or RIB for slow-cooked beef ribs. After dinner, walk to Fuglen - a vintage Norwegian café-bar for a nightcap

directions: Take E6 north from Oslo through Gudbrandsdalen valley
Stop at Ringebu Stave Church (quick detour off E6)
Continue to Sjoa River for family rafting
Follow RV15 west to Lom

stops.name: Ringebu Stave Church
stops.desc: Built c.1220 in Gudbrandsdalen valley. Medieval interior with original furnishings

stops.name: Sjoa River rafting
stops.desc: 11 km gentle rafting on Sjoa River. Guide, wetsuit, gear included. Class 1-2 rapids

stops.name: Lom Stave Church
stops.desc: Built c.1158. One of Norway's largest stave churches. Open May–Sep

stops.name: Fossheim Bakeri
stops.desc: Norway's best bakery - famous kanelboller and bread

activities.desc: Mild whitewater on Sjoa River. Guide, wetsuit included. Class 1-2 rapids - suitable for beginners
Norway's best bakery - famous kanelboller and bread
Charming mountain village. Walk along the Bøvra River and explore the historic center
Flat course right in Lom village. Quick round for disc golf enthusiasts

groupNotes: Longest drive day but broken up with stops along the Gudbrandsdalen valley. Ringebu Stave Church is a quick detour off E6. The Sjoa River rafting center offers class 1-2 trips. Arrive Lom in the afternoon; Medalen Disc Golf is a free flat course right in the village. Fossheim Bakeri has Norway's best kanelboller - a great spot for pastries and coffee.

lodging.name: Nordal Turistsenter
lodging.pros: Affordable cabin-style lodging, kitchen facilities, central Lom location near church, family-friendly
lodging.cons: Basic amenities, no restaurant on site, older cabins, thin walls

lodging.name: Fossheim Hotel
lodging.pros: Historic hotel right in Lom center, cozy atmosphere, good restaurant with local lamb, across from Lom Stave Church
lodging.cons: No pool or spa, limited parking, older building with some small rooms

lodging.name: Røisheim Hotel
lodging.pros: Historic 1800s timber manor, exceptional Norwegian farm-to-table restaurant, unique traditional decor, serene setting
lodging.cons: Very expensive for the area, limited availability, no modern amenities like pool

meals.lunch: Sjoa Rafting Center cafe - burgers, coffee, and Kvikk Lunsj for the road, or pack from Matkroken in Otta
meals.dinner: Fossheim Hotel restaurant - traditional Gudbrandsdalen lamb stew and local beer in a cozy 1830s timber building. After dinner, walk across the street to see Lom Stave Church lit up at night

directions: Take RV15 from Lom heading northwest
Turn onto RV63 at Grotli towards Geiranger
Stop at Dalsnibba Skywalk (toll road) before descending
Descend Geirangervegen (RV63) into Geiranger village - stunning mountain switchbacks

stops.name: Dalsnibba Skywalk
stops.desc: 1,500m viewpoint over Geirangerfjord. Europe's highest fjord view by road

stops.name: Flydalsjuvet viewpoint
stops.desc: Iconic photo spot looking down Geirangerfjord. The classic postcard view

activities.desc: 1,500m above the fjord. Unbelievable views over the entire Geirangerfjord
The classic Geirangerfjord postcard photo
UNESCO World Heritage fjord. The Seven Sisters and Friaren waterfalls. Lunch on board
Walk BEHIND a waterfall. Easy-moderate trail from Geiranger

groupNotes: Epic drive day - Dalsnibba and Flydalsjuvet are quick photo stops as you approach from the south. The fjord cruise is the afternoon highlight. Evening: explore Geiranger village.

lodging.name: Grande Fjord Hotel
lodging.pros: More affordable Geiranger option, quieter location 5 min from center, fjord views from many rooms, free parking
lodging.cons: No elevator, older building, less well-known than other Geiranger hotels, basic breakfast

lodging.name: Hotel Geiranger
lodging.pros: Classic Norwegian fjord hotel, panoramic dining room, central Geiranger location, excellent breakfast and dinner buffet
lodging.cons: Limited parking, peak season crowds, no pool or spa

lodging.name: Hotel Union Geiranger
lodging.pros: Historic 1891 property with full spa, indoor/outdoor pools, stunning fjord panorama, award-winning breakfast, gardens
lodging.cons: Very expensive, large hotel, some rooms need renovation

meals.lunch: Café onboard the fjord cruise - salmon wrap
meals.dinner: Brasserie Posten at Hotel Union - Norwegian seafood platter, reindeer fillet, cloudberries for dessert with panoramic Geirangerfjord views. After dinner, use the Hotel Union spa (pools, sauna) or sit on the terrace with a nightcap

activities.desc: High-speed RIB boat through Geirangerfjord. Get right next to the Seven Sisters waterfall
Stillwater kayak on the fjord. Paddle right under the waterfalls. Suitable for all skill levels
Historic road with 11 hairpins and a panoramic fjord viewpoint at the top
Farm trail above Geiranger. Stunning fjord views from the meadow. Easy walk
Abandoned mountain farm perched 250m above the fjord. Moderate fitness

groupNotes: Full day in Geiranger. Morning: RIB safari. Afternoon: choose between kayaking the fjord or hiking Skageflå. Evening: dinner followed by a casual Eagle Road sunset drive.

lodging.name: Grande Fjord Hotel
lodging.pros: More affordable Geiranger option, quieter location 5 min from center, fjord views from many rooms, free parking
lodging.cons: No elevator, older building, less well-known than other Geiranger hotels, basic breakfast

lodging.name: Hotel Geiranger
lodging.pros: Classic Norwegian fjord hotel, panoramic dining room, central Geiranger location, excellent breakfast and dinner buffet
lodging.cons: Limited parking, peak season crowds, no pool or spa

lodging.name: Hotel Union Geiranger
lodging.pros: Historic 1891 property with full spa, indoor/outdoor pools, stunning fjord panorama, award-winning breakfast, gardens
lodging.cons: Very expensive, large hotel, some rooms need renovation

meals.lunch: Westerås Farm café - local goat cheese waffles and berry jam with fjord views
meals.dinner: Naustkroa Café in the village - traditional Norwegian fish soup and local craft beer by the Geiranger waterfront. After dinner, walk down to the fjord shore for sunset photos

directions: Take Ørnevegen (RV63) up from Geiranger
Continue RV63 north through Valldal valley
Cross Trollstigen mountain pass (typically open for the summer season)
If Trollstigen is bypassed or unpassable, utilize the standard scenic Fv650 directly to Ålesund
Continue to Ålesund via E136 + E39

stops.name: Trollstigen Viewpoint
stops.desc: Dramatic viewing platform cantilevered over the mountain. 11 hairpin turns below

stops.name: Gudbrandsjuvet Gorge
stops.desc: Spectacular river gorge with metal walkways over the churning water

activities.desc: Legendary mountain road with 11 hairpin turns. Cantilevered viewing platform. Iconic Norway
Walkways suspended over a raging river gorge
Climb 418 steps to Ålesund's panoramic city viewpoint. Sweeping views over the archipelago
Self-guided walk through Europe's most complete Art Nouveau city center

groupNotes: The Trollstigen drive is a bucket-list experience. Safe rockfall protection infrastructure has significantly stabilized access seasons. If choosing to bypass, Fv650 provides a direct and highly scenic connection. Evening: walk up Aksla - 418 steps to the city viewpoint.

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Ålesund
lodging.pros: Reliable chain, excellent breakfast included, central Ålesund location near harbor, free Wi-Fi
lodging.cons: Basic rooms, chain hotel character, no unique features

lodging.name: Quality Hotel Ålesund
lodging.pros: Modern waterfront hotel, spacious rooms, good breakfast, harbor views, near Art Nouveau center
lodging.cons: Slightly out of the old town, can feel corporate, no pool

lodging.name: Hotel Brosundet
lodging.pros: Stunning waterfront boutique hotel in historic Art Nouveau building, exceptional restaurant, cozy atmosphere, harbor views
lodging.cons: Pricey, limited parking, no pool or spa, some rooms small

meals.lunch: Valldal strawberry farm café - fresh strawberry cake
meals.dinner: XL Diner - classic Norwegian seafood. Try the bacalao (dried salted cod stew - an Ålesund specialty since the Portuguese trade days), or the fresh catch of the day. After dinner, climb the 418 steps to Aksla viewpoint for the midnight panorama

activities.desc: One of Scandinavia's largest aquariums. Huge ocean tank, penguins, seals
Paddle Ålesund's inner canals right through the city center. Stillwater
Short but steep hike to a granite peak (314m). 360° views over Ålesund and the Atlantic
Drive to Godøya island. Climb the lighthouse. Rugged Atlantic coast views
Harborside brewery in a historic pier building

groupNotes: Flex day in Ålesund. Morning: Atlantic Sea Park. Afternoon: choose between kayaking the canals or hiking Sukkertoppen. Late afternoon: Alnes Lighthouse. Evening: Molo Brew taproom.

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Ålesund
lodging.pros: Reliable chain, excellent breakfast included, central Ålesund location near harbor, free Wi-Fi
lodging.cons: Basic rooms, chain hotel character, no unique features

lodging.name: Quality Hotel Ålesund
lodging.pros: Modern waterfront hotel, spacious rooms, good breakfast, harbor views, near Art Nouveau center
lodging.cons: Slightly out of the old town, can feel corporate, no pool

lodging.name: Hotel Brosundet
lodging.pros: Stunning waterfront boutique hotel in historic Art Nouveau building, exceptional restaurant, cozy atmosphere, harbor views
lodging.cons: Pricey, limited parking, no pool or spa, some rooms small

meals.lunch: Café at Atlanterhavsparken - fish and chips with Atlantic views
meals.dinner: Apotekergata No. 5 - modern Norwegian shared plates in a historic Art Nouveau building. Great cocktails and local craft beer. After dinner, take a twilight stroll through the Art Nouveau streets to admire the spire-lit skyline

directions: Take E39 north from Ålesund towards Vestnes
Take the Vestnes–Molde ferry across the Moldefjord
Arrive in Molde and drive directly up to the Varden viewpoint

stops.name: Molde panorama viewpoint
stops.desc: Varden - 407m overlooking 222 mountain peaks across the Moldefjord. Exceptional panoramic overview.

activities.desc: Scenic cruise across the wide fjord. Grab a traditional svele pancake in the galley.
Famous 407m viewpoint over Molde, the Romsdal Alps, and 222 mountain peaks across the fjord.
Stroll through the town center park and town hall roof garden to see why it is called the Town of Roses.

groupNotes: A light transit day making a clean forward progress northward. Drive smoothly onto the ferry at Vestnes. Spend a relaxed afternoon exploring Molde town and check the iconic mountain views from Varden before dinner.

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Moldefjord
lodging.pros: Reliable chain hotel, excellent breakfast, central Molde location near harbor, good value
lodging.cons: Basic rooms, no unique atmosphere, no pool

lodging.name: Molde Fjordhotell
lodging.pros: Fjord-view rooms, central location, good restaurant, rooftop terrace with panoramic Molde panorama
lodging.cons: Older building, some rooms dated, basic amenities

lodging.name: Scandic Seilet Hotel
lodging.pros: Iconic sail-shaped tower dominating Molde skyline, stunning 360-degree views from upper floors, modern rooms, excellent breakfast
lodging.cons: A bit out of the old town, large conference hotel, windy location

meals.lunch: Lunch in Ålesund before departing or onboard the ferry
meals.dinner: Glass Restaurant at Scandic Seilet - floor-to-ceiling Moldefjord views. Try the bacalao or pan-seared halibut. After dinner, view the late-night sky from the waterfront.

directions: Drive north from Molde on RV64 through the Atlantic Ocean Tunnel to Averøy
Drive the iconic Atlantic Ocean Road across the 8 bridges
Stop at Kvernes Stave Church on Averøy island
Take the Kanestraum–Halsa ferry along the E39 route
Continue north along E39/E6 directly into Trondheim

stops.name: Atlantic Ocean Road viewpoints
stops.desc: 8 stunning bridges connecting islands over the open Atlantic. Stop at Eldhusøya for the elevated walkway.

stops.name: Kvernes Stave Church
stops.desc: Beautiful 14th-century stave church on Averøy overlooking the Kvernesfjord.

activities.desc: One of the world's most scenic drives. 8.3 km across islands with dramatic bridges.
Ferry transit connecting sections of coastal E39.
Trondheim's most charming neighborhood. Colorful wooden houses, cobblestone streets.

groupNotes: An incredible transit flow up the coast. Moving the Atlantic Road to today eliminates all back-tracking loops. Stop at Eldhusøya rest area for the safest and most cinematic photos. Catch the Kanestraum ferry and enter Trondheim seamlessly from the west.

lodging.name: City Living Schøller Hotel
lodging.pros: Self-catering apartments with kitchenette, central Trondheim location near Bakklandet, affordable for groups
lodging.cons: No restaurant, no daily housekeeping, basic facilities, check-in at separate location

lodging.name: Clarion Hotel Trondheim
lodging.pros: Modern harborfront hotel, excellent breakfast, rooftop bar with views, close to Nidaros Cathedral and Bakklandet
lodging.cons: Parking expensive, busy with business travelers on weekdays

lodging.name: Radisson Blu Royal Garden
lodging.pros: Central Trondheim location, large comfortable rooms, indoor pool and sauna, extensive breakfast buffet, attached to shopping center
lodging.cons: Large chain hotel, impersonal feel, some rooms face interior atrium

meals.lunch: Pack lunch or stop at a seaside café near Kristiansund
meals.dinner: Bakklandet Skydsstation - cozy historic inn on Bakklandet cobblestone street. Reindeer stew with lingonberry jam, fresh salmon, or local specialty flatbreads. Walk across the Old Town Bridge afterward.

activities.desc: Crown jewels, rose window, crypt
17th-century fortress. Cannons, city views, Resistance Museum

activities.text: Rockheim - National Museum of Pop Music
activities.desc: Interactive music museum. Hands-on exhibits, recording studios
Shopping and coffee in Trondheim's most photogenic neighborhood
Trondheim Torg and independent boutiques in Bakklandet

groupNotes: Full city day in Trondheim. Morning: Nidaros Cathedral. Mid-day: Rockheim museum - interactive music exhibits. Afternoon: choose between exploring Kristiansten Fortress or shopping in Bakklandet. Evening: farewell dinner.

lodging.name: City Living Schøller Hotel
lodging.pros: Self-catering apartments with kitchenette, central Trondheim location near Bakklandet, affordable for groups
lodging.cons: No restaurant, no daily housekeeping, basic facilities, check-in at separate location

lodging.name: Clarion Hotel Trondheim
lodging.pros: Modern harborfront hotel, excellent breakfast, rooftop bar with views, close to Nidaros Cathedral and Bakklandet
lodging.cons: Parking expensive, busy with business travelers on weekdays

lodging.name: Radisson Blu Royal Garden
lodging.pros: Central Trondheim location, large comfortable rooms, indoor pool and sauna, extensive breakfast buffet, attached to shopping center
lodging.cons: Large chain hotel, impersonal feel, some rooms face interior atrium

meals.lunch: Kaffebrenneriet Bakklandet - best coffee and fresh pastries on the cobblestone street
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Fagn (Michelin-starred modern Norwegian tasting menu) or Speilsalen. End the trip at Trondheim Mikrobryggeri for a final local craft beer.

activities.desc: CEST → EDT (-6h). Connect via major European hubs. Return to regional destination terminal.
Last walk through Bakklandet, coffee at Kaffebrenneriet, or local exploration.
Aquavit, brunost, Norwegian wool

groupNotes: Departure day from Trondheim (TRD). Most US connections route through Amsterdam or Copenhagen. Ensure bags are checked completely through.

meals.lunch: Airport lounge or grab sandwiches for the plane
